title: fix(metadata-admin): inspector selects stop flagging a valid value while their option roster loads (objectui#8862)
body:
Fixes #8862

`InspectorSelectField` decided "this stored value is not offered" by testing membership in the `options` array it was handed, and **that array cannot say why it is empty**. An async picker mid-round-trip hands over `[]`, indistinguishable from a catalog that genuinely does not carry the value — so for the length of a fetch a correctly bound key rendered under a marker asserting it does not exist, then settled to the right label. On the metadata-authoring surface that marker is a claim about the author's own data, and the plausible response to it is to re-author a binding that was already right.

## The judgement this card was dispatched for: fix the primitive, once

The card left open whether to repair the primitive or each call site. Measured first (see **Population** below): every call site that reaches the defect gets its roster from a loader that **already publishes a `loading` of its own**, so the primitive-level repair costs each call site one word and closes the class for the sites that do not exist yet. The comment that already sat inside `InspectorSelectField` — "closing it needs a loading contract this primitive does not have" — asked for exactly this, and it is replaced rather than left to read as live.

`loading` makes the primitive's answer a **tri-state**:

| roster | stored value | trigger renders |
|:--|:--|:--|
| answered | offered | the option's own label |
| answered | **not** offered | the value under `unknownValueLabel` (unchanged) |
| **not answered** | anything | the value, **bare** |

The synthesised row still renders in the pending arm. Withholding it would put back the blank trigger objectui#8488 removed, and would blank it exactly when the author has least other evidence of what is stored; only the **claim** is withheld. A value drawn plainly asserts nothing about a roster that has not spoken.

⚠️ That is not the direction objectui#8488 refused. What it refused — "stored" and "offered" drawn alike — is a claim about a roster that **has** answered and can tell them apart. This one cannot, yet.

The prop is spelled `loading` because the sibling atom `InspectorComboField` in the same family already spells the same signal that way, and the two get swapped for one another at call sites.

## Population — re-measured, and the card's list needed one correction

Every `InspectorSelectField` call site in the tree was classified by whether its roster is asynchronous and whether the select is actually mounted while that roster is empty.

**Fixed — reaches the defect (3 sites, 4 controls):**

- `ViewColumnInspector`'s field-key picker (`useObjectFields`) — the reported reproduction. Its gate is `fieldOptions.length > 0 || currentFieldKey !== ''`, so a stored key keeps the picker mounted through the round trip.
- `ReportDefaultInspector`'s dataset binding (`useDatasetCatalog`) — same shape of gate (`catalog.datasets.length > 0 || datasetName`).
- Both of that inspector's chart axes (`useDatasetSemantics`), which have no gate at all beyond a chart type being set. `DatasetNamesEditor` at the very same call site already consumed `semantics.loading`; the axes did not.

**Left alone, with the reason:**

- ⭐ **`ActionTargetField` (`useMetaOptions`) does NOT reach the defect** — the card named it and this run measures otherwise. Its `usePicker = !!metaType && options.length > 0` renders an `InspectorTextField` while the roster is empty, so the select never mounts during the round trip and there is no marker to withhold. Threading the prop there would be dead code. The same length gate immunises `ObjectPicker`, `FieldPicker` (`ActionDefaultInspector`) and `ObjectPickerField` / `FieldPickerField` (`PageBlockInspector`).
- Every other `InspectorSelectField` call site takes a **synchronous** roster — a constant list, a spec enum, or draft data already in hand (`AppNavInspector`, `FlowEdgeInspector`, `FlowNodeInspector`, `FlowNodeConfigField`, `ViewVariantInspector`, `DatasetDefaultInspector`, `ObjectFieldInspector`, `HookDefaultInspector`, `studio-design/ObjectGroupInspector`).
- The async rosters that are neither of those go to `InspectorComboField`, which has no absence marker to withhold in the first place.

## Still open, deliberately

A roster whose fetch **FAILED** also resolves to an empty array, with `loading` back to false — so the marker still fires on a load error. objectui#5170 ruled that arm for the SchemaForm widget family and chose a dedicated failure surface over a silent empty roster. Answering it on this primitive is a decision about what a picker owes its host, not a spelling, so it is filed rather than guessed. See **Acceptance notes**.

## The pin witnesses the transient frame, not the settled one

The defect exists **only while the request is in flight**, so a case that renders a populated roster and finds no marker is green on the defect and on the fix alike. Two suites, at two altitudes:

- `_shared.rosterPending.test.tsx` — the primitive's tri-state, handed `loading` directly. Holds the roster in the state the bug needs and reads the rendered **trigger** (the defect was entirely in what reached pixels). Includes the transition in one mount, and the true negative: **answered** roster without the value ⇒ the marker is still there.
- `ViewColumnInspector.rosterPending.test.tsx` — the whole chain, driving the real `useObjectFields` against a metadata client whose promise is **held open**, so the in-flight frame is readable. A fix to the primitive with the prop unthreaded at this call site is green in the first suite and still ships the defect; this one is the seam.

⛔ `ViewColumnInspector.identityRead.test.tsx` already asserts `'name (not in object)'` is absent, and **it is green on the defect**: its draft binds no object, so `useObjectFields` short-circuits and reports `loading: false` on the first render (answered-and-empty, not unanswered), and its legacy column yields no field key at all, so the control it reads is an `input` rather than the combobox. Triage asked for this to be established before touching the primitive; it covers the retired-alias read and says nothing about this window.

## Reverse verification — two legs, from the committed fix

Each leg mutates, **proves the mutation reached disk** (removed-marker count 0 / injected-marker count at least 1, plus the file's hash), runs, restores with `git checkout HEAD --`, and proves the restore by hash equality against the HEAD blob. A trap on `EXIT INT TERM` restores on any interruption; the final tree diff against HEAD is empty. Predicted direction was *turns red*, and the informative part is the **asymmetry**, not the redness.

**Leg A — ablate the primitive's read** (restore `label: unknownValueLabel(current)` unconditionally, i.e. the pre-fix source):

- RED: all five pending-arm rows of the primitive suite, plus both in-flight rows of the end-to-end suite.
- GREEN, unchanged: the primitive suite's three answered-arm rows (true negative, partially-arrived roster, the empty state), and the end-to-end suite's true negative.

**Leg B — ablate only the call-site seam** (drop `loading={fieldsLoading}` from `ViewColumnInspector`, primitive untouched):

- GREEN: the entire primitive suite — which is the point, and why the second suite exists.
- RED: both in-flight rows of the end-to-end suite. Its true negative stays green.

⭐ **One measurement changed a test.** On the first ablation the end-to-end true negative read the in-flight frame before landing the roster, so leg A turned it red **for the pending frame's reason** and it stopped being able to testify about the answered one. Both legs failing on a single ablation is exactly what a true negative exists to rule out, so that case was decoupled (a second commit, with the reason recorded on it); the readings above are from the re-run.

Read on the final commit, `177c6ab42`. Repo-wide scans belong to CI.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations from this file surface, recorded here and not filed by this PR:

1. **To file — the load-FAILURE arm of the same blindness.** A failed roster fetch leaves `options` empty with `loading` false, so a valid stored value is still flagged "(not in object)" / "(not found)", permanently rather than briefly. Distinct from objectui#5170, which ruled the failure arm for the SchemaForm **widget** family and is not about this primitive. Dedupe words: `InspectorSelectField` · load failure · empty roster · unknown value · `PickerLoadFailure`.
2. **To file — the markers on this primitive's designer call sites are hard-coded English.** `ViewColumnInspector` passes `` `${v} (not in object)` `` as a literal while `engine.form.notInObject` exists in the catalogue in both locales and is consumed by `widgets.tsx`; `ViewVariantInspector` ("(not found)") and `FlowNodeConfigField` ("(deprecated)") are the same shape. A zh-CN author reads untranslated text on a translated surface. Dedupe words: `unknownValueLabel` · `notInObject` · designer marker · untranslated literal · inspector i18n.
3. **Noted, not filed:** while the roster is out and *no* value is stored, `ViewColumnInspector` renders a text input and flips to a combobox when the roster lands — a control-type change, not a false claim, and nothing about it is wrong on screen. Carrier for a later pass: whoever next touches `showFieldPicker`. Also noted: `InspectorComboField` draws "Loading…" for an empty value while loading where `InspectorSelectField` draws its placeholder; changing that would move objectui#8450's pinned empty state and buys nothing this card is about.
